newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama to draft homeland for largest Indian group.
newsitem.headline: Panama to draft homeland for largest Indian group.

text.p: Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares on Thursday appointed a government commission to draft a sovereign homeland for the nation's largest Indian group, a presidential spokeswoman said.
Leaders of the Ngobe-Bugle Indians, the largest of six Indian groups with a population of 125,000, have been pressing for an Indian territory, or comarca, for 25 years.
"The president appointed the commission of government officials and Indian leaders which has 30 days to report back with a boundary for the comarca," the spokeswoman said.
Ngobe-Bugle Indians this week ended a 250-mile (400-km) march across Panama to demand an end to copper mining on their lands and a sovereign homeland.

They object to a local unit of Canadian mining firm Tiomin Resources Inc operating a copper mining project in Cerro Colorado, 220 miles (350 km) from Panama City. Company officials said they planned to continue the project.
